section: Financial instabilities - crises, systemic risk, shadow banking, macroprudential regulation

accepted.s: Which of the following risks was flagged in the Financial Stability Report released in June 2026?
o: Risk from falling foreign exchange reserves
accepted.x: The June 2026 Financial Stability Report flagged risks associated with unsecured lending through fintech platforms.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the specific risk associated with the named report and date.

accepted.s: The Financial Stability Report of June 2026 highlighted fintech-related risk primarily in the area of:
accepted.x: The report highlighted risks arising from fintech unsecured lending, rather than from secured housing finance or the other listed areas.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related forms of lending.

accepted.s: The credit-deposit ratio of Andhra Pradesh was reported as 157.40 per cent. What does this most directly indicate?
o: The State had no dependence on bank deposits for lending.
Banks accepted 157.40 per cent more deposits than they lent.
Bank lending was very high relative to deposits.
Deposits were 157.40 per cent of bank credit.
accepted.x: A credit-deposit ratio of 157.40 per cent indicates that lending was very high relative to deposits in Andhra Pradesh. It does not mean that deposits exceeded credit.
accepted.tq: Interpret the direction and meaning of a ratio rather than reversing its numerator and denominator.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the regulatory arrangement in the Indian financial system?
o: IRDAI regulates banks and NBFCs, while RBI regulates insurers and FSDC regulates only stock exchanges.
RBI regulates banks and NBFCs, IRDAI regulates insurers, and FSDC coordinates among financial regulators.
RBI regulates insurers, IRDAI regulates banks and NBFCs, and FSDC regulates all financial institutions.
FSDC independently regulates banks, NBFCs and insurers, while RBI performs only a coordinating role.
accepted.x: The RBI regulates banks and NBFCs, IRDAI regulates insurers, and the Financial Stability and Development Council coordinates among the financial regulators. FSDC is a coordinating body rather than the direct regulator of all these entities.
accepted.tq: Compare the regulator associated with each segment and distinguish regulation from coordination.
